With reference to the attached translation and the
instructions of the D.C. (Special Branch) thereon, the
undersigned called on Mr. Tao Loh-jing (陶樂勤), editor of
the "Shanghai Public Daily News" (市民日報) on May 10 and
asked him to name the gangsters to whom he refers and lodge
his complaint.
In reply, Mr. Tao stated that the Chinese Ratepayers'
Association has received many complaints about the activities
of gangsters in the International Settlement, of which the
most serious one was the robbery in the Nanking Road Branch
of the Bank of Communications which was committed in broad
daylight and in the heart of the business centre.
The "Shanghai Public Daily News", whose office is now
in No.4, Lane 587, Yu Ya Ching Road, was established in 1933
by Messrs. Lieu Chung-yin (刘仲英) and Kuh Foh-dien (葛福田),
committeemen of the Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation.
On September 26, 1936, the publisher of the paper
was fined $20 by the Shanghai First Special District Court for
non-registration. Since then it secured registration
certificates No.1755 from the Ministry of Interior and No.1044
from the Central Propaganda Department.
This paper has been losing money since its initial
publication in 1933; its circulation is very low although it is
claimed to be a semi-official organ of the Shanghai First
Special District Citizens' Federation.
With the assistance of Messrs. Yu Ya-ching (虞洽卿),

May 3, 1937. Morning Translation

Shanghai Public Daily News (市民日报) published the following editorial comment on May 1 :-

A STUDY OF THE S.M.C. FINANCIAL ADMINISTRATION

The S.M.C's financial position has always been a sound one. The regular revenue of the Council has been on the rise since 1912. If we indicate the increase by numerals, the number for 1912, say 100, has been increased to 638 in 1936. The rise in the Council's expenditure, however, has been even faster than that of its revenue. If we also indicate this rise by numerals, the number for 1912, say 100, has been increased to 806 in 1936. This shows that the revenue of the Council does not correspond with its expenditure.

The rise in the expenditure may be attributed to (1) inflation of currency and increase in the price of commodities, (2) social causes, such as the swelling of the ranks of unemployed and the issue of a relief fund, and (3) reasons of its own, such as reckless expenditure. It is to be noted that the increase in the Council's expenditure is not so much a result of items (1) and (2), but is actually due to the extravagant use of public funds by the official administering the finance who has failed to spend the money, received from the residents in the Settlement, in the quarters that are most profitable to the public. This is because in the past the price of commodities was on the decline due to depression and also because the Council had not carried out any particular project for the welfare of the poor.

The unnecessary expenses of the S.M.C. include the Police expenditure, the upkeep of the Orchestra, Exchange Compensation and Passage Allowances. The rate-payers are not benefited by the issue of Passage Allowances, Orchestra upkeep and Exchange Compensation. It is the small number of foreign employees of the Council who receive the benefit. Since 1931 the money expended on the Municipal Orchestra amounts to $1,900,000; the Exchange Compensation issued amounts to more than $10,000,000, while Passage Allowances for foreign employees cost several hundred thousand dollars. Even those who have no knowledge of finance will realise that such expenses should be dispensed with.

As for the Police expenditure, its increase is out of all proportion. The Police expenditure in 1912 can be represented by the figure 100; in 1936 the figure increases to 822. Between 1928 and 1931, the increase was most rapid. In 1928, the expenditure was $4,608,156, but in 1931 it increased to $9,629,608. In spite of this, there has been no improvement in the peace and safety of the International Settlement. The worst state of affairs was in 1932 when the International Settlement was used as a base of operations for warfare. In ordinary times, policemen are used for arresting petty hawkers and beggars only. Now they are to be used to protect the workers who will demolish straw huts, which are not unlawful, and to prevent hut dwellers from protecting their own property. The armed demonstrations and the notorious gangsters, who constitute a menace to the peace and safety of the Settlement, are allowed to remain.

In conclusion, we request the S.M.C. authorities to use the money in a way most beneficial to the public.

1937年5月3日。晨间译文

《市民日报》于5月1日发表了以下社论评论：

工部局财政管理研究

工部局的财务状况一向良好。自1912年以来，工部局的常规收入一直在增长。如果用数字表示增长幅度，以1912年为100，则1936年增至638。然而，工部局支出的增长速度甚至快于收入的增长。如果也用数字表示这一增长，以1912年为100，则1936年增至806。这表明工部局的收入与其支出不相称。

支出的增加可归因于：(1) 货币通货膨胀和商品价格上涨；(2) 社会原因，如失业队伍膨胀和救济基金的发放；以及 (3) 自身原因，如挥霍性支出。值得注意的是，工部局支出的增加并非主要源于第(1)和(2)项，而实际上是由于负责财政管理的官员挥霍公款，未能将从租界居民那里收取的资金用于对公众最有益的领域。这是因为过去由于经济萧条，商品价格呈下降趋势，而且工部局也没有实施任何特别有利于穷人的项目。

工部局的不必要开支包括警务支出、乐队维持费、汇兑补偿和差旅津贴。租界纳税人并未从发放差旅津贴、乐队维持费和汇兑补偿中受益。受益者是工部局少数外籍雇员。自1931年以来，花费在市立乐队上的金额达190万元；发出的汇兑补偿超过1000万元，而外籍雇员的差旅津贴也耗资数十万元。即使是不懂财务的人也会意识到，这些开支应当取消。

至于警务支出，其增长完全不成比例。1912年的警务支出可用数字100表示；1936年该数字增至822。1928年至1931年间，增长最为迅速。1928年，支出为4,608,156元，但1931年增至9,629,608元。尽管如此，公共租界的治安状况并无改善。最糟糕的情况出现在1932年，当时公共租界被用作战争行动的基地。在平时，警察仅用于逮捕小贩和乞丐。现在，他们却被用来保护那些将拆除并非非法的草棚的工人，并阻止棚屋居民保护自己的财产。而那些武装示威者和臭名昭著的流氓团伙，构成了对租界和平与安全的威胁，却任由其存在。

总之，我们请求工部局当局以最有利于公众的方式使用资金。

Shanghai Public Daily News publishes the following article:

POLICE OFFICERS FORCE PAYMENT OF MUNICIPAL RATES

The 9th District Branch of the First Special
District Citizens' Federation has received the following
complaint from one of its members giving the address of the
Chengtu Wine Shop (成都酒店):- "During the past several
days, Police officers have called at various shops and
demanded that the inmates should pay the Municipal Rates
which are in arrears. What is worse is that they went
in and out of the rooms of tenants or up the stairs at will
and forced the tenants to secure money immediately to meet
the payment of the Municipal Rates."
Owing to trade depression as well as financial
stringency, the residents may not be able to pay the
Municipal Rates at the appointed date. If the S.M.C. can
no longer tolerate the non-payment of Municipal Rates by
the residents of the Settlement, it should take legal
proceedings against them. It is indeed a matter of deep
regret that Police officers whose duty it is to secure the
safety of the public should resort to improper methods
to enforce payment of Municipal Rates.
The 9th District Branch is understood to have
referred the matter to the Citizens' Federation as well as
the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, and requested them
to open negotiations with the S.M.C. according to law.
It is said that those who have been threatened and forced
to pay the Municipal Rates are also expected to report to
the Federation so as to facilitate its negotiations with
the S.M.C..

with editor）

《市民日报》刊登以下文章：

警员强迫缴纳市政捐税

上海第一特区市民联合会第九区分会收到其一名会员的如下投诉，地址为成都酒店：“过去几天，警员走访各家店铺，要求店内人员缴纳拖欠的市政捐税。更糟糕的是，他们随意进出租户房间或上下楼梯，强迫租户立即筹款以支付市政捐税。”
由于商业萧条以及资金紧张，居民可能无法在指定日期缴纳市政捐税。如果工部局不能再容忍租界居民拖欠市政捐税，应通过法律程序对他们提起诉讼。令人深感遗憾的是，职责在于保障公共安全的警员竟采取不当手段强制征收市政捐税。
据悉，第九区分会已将此事提交给市民联合会及华人纳税会，并要求他们依法与工部局进行谈判。据说，那些受到威胁并被迫缴纳市政捐税的人也被期望向联合会报告，以便其与工部局进行谈判。

（批注：与编辑交涉）

Translation of dispatch No. 9238
from the Shanghai First Special
Area District Court to the Legal
Dept., Shanghai Municipal Council

We received a dispatch Character Chung No.955 from
the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, which stated:
"We are in receipt of an order No.19821 from
the Shanghai City Government, which stated:
According to a dispatch No.3832 dated
July 11, 1936, received from the Ministry
of Interior, it is stated:
According to dispatch No.2189 dated
July 6, 1936, received from the Central
Propaganda Bureau, it is stated:
'The Dah Bah News Agency (大白新聞社)
the Citizens' Daily (市民日報社 ) and the
Ningpo Daily (寧波日報社) have up to the
present time failed to send in their
publications for examination. They
have committed a contempt of the law
and ordinances. They should be fined
according to Article 31 of the Press
Law. You are hereby requested to act
accordingly.'
The Dah Bah News Agency has long failed
to send their publications for examination.
We have, on March 27th of this year, sent a
dispatch No.1363 to your Honorable Government
to take up this matter and to instruct your
subordinates to act accordingly. In view of
the dispatch quoted above, since these news
agencies have not yet complied with the order,
this is indeed not proper. Naturally, they
should be punished according to the law. We
beg to communicate with you per this dispatch.
Kindly act immediately in accordance with the
law and favor us with a reply.

我们收到上海市公安局发来的中字第九五五号公函，内容如下：
“我们收到上海市政府发来的第一九八二一号命令，内容如下：
根据1936年7月11日收到的内政部第三八三二号公函，内容如下：
根据1936年7月6日收到的中央宣传部第二一八九号公函，内容如下：
‘大白新闻社、市民日报社及宁波日报社截至目前仍未送交出版物供审查。其行为已构成对法律法规的蔑视。应根据《出版法》第三十一条处以罚款。请据此办理。’
大白新闻社长期未送交出版物供审查。我们曾于今年3月27日向贵政府发出第一三六三号公函，提请处理此事并指示下属部门据此办理。鉴于上述公函，既然这些新闻机构尚未服从命令，此举实属不当。自然应依法予以处罚。特此函达。请立即依法办理并复函。”

A_ STUDY OF THE S.M.eC. FINANCIAL ADMINISTRATION 


The S$.M.C's financial position has always 
been a sound one. The regular revenue of the Council 
has been on the rise since 1912. If we indicate the 
increase by numerals, the number for 1912, say 100, has 
been increased to 638 in 1936. The rise in the Council's

not correspond with its expenditure.
